summary: Frontend-only regression + new Go Live features test. All new testids present (station-id, schedule-input, arm-schedule, scheduled, cancel-schedule, reconnecting, listeners). Arm/Start disabled-state logic works exactly per spec. Schedule arm → shows 'Armed for ... · in N min' with cancel; cancel returns to datetime input. Regression: license flow, playlist create, WAV upload via [data-testid=add-files-input], and play all initialized without exceptions. No real broadcast triggered.

issues: React hydration warning: <span> inside <option> at PlayerBar.js:395-396 (crossfade select). Pre-existing dev-instrumentation wrapper issue, not from this GoLive refactor. Recommend main agent clean up if it appears in production build.

critical_code_review_comments: GoLiveModal.js line 275: Arm button disabled logic uses `!canGo || !scheduleInput` which correctly requires host+port+password AND datetime. Consistent with spec.
Schedule arm rejects past/invalid times silently (line 81 `if (!ts || ts <= Date.now()) return;`) — consider surfacing a user-visible message if a past time is entered.
station-id polling every 15s is fine; poll only runs while `live` is true and stationId non-empty — good gating.
Pre-existing PlayerBar `<option>` hydration warning is unrelated to this GoLive refactor but flagged for cleanup.
seed_data_creation: Created a Test Playlist and a small generated /tmp/test.wav for regression only (client-side only).
context_for_next_testing_agent: All Go Live modal enhancements (station-id field, schedule arm/cancel, reconnecting placeholder, listeners badge testid) verified present and validated. Arm disabled when either password empty OR datetime empty; enabled only when BOTH set with future date. Start disabled when password empty OR host empty. Cancel schedule returns UI to datetime input. Playback regression clean (no critical console errors). Did NOT test actual scheduled fire (would require waiting) or real broadcast (explicitly forbidden). Pre-existing hydration warning from PlayerBar `<option>` present but not caused by this change.
rca of the issue: No issues found in this test iteration.
